# Aha Dispute & Point Reversal

## Dispute Types
- Points not credited within the expected window.
- Clawbacks applied for referrals or wins.
- Redemption not delivered.

## Process
Raise a dispute in the portal under My Points > Raise Dispute with the
transaction reference. SLA is 5 business days.

## Point Reversal
Points are reversed where the underlying transaction is reversed: referral
exit within six months or invalidated cross-sell wins.

## Appeals
Unresolved disputes escalate to the Rewards & Recognition team with a
30-day review window.

Policy code: AHA-DIS-2026-01 | Owner: Rewards & Recognition team.

# Aha FAQ

## Common Questions
Q: How do I check my balance?
A: The dashboard shows the current balance and the next expiring tranche.

Q: Can I transfer points?
A: No, points are non-transferable. Giving to approved causes is supported.

Q: What if I leave the bank?
A: Unredeemed points lapse on the last working day. Redeem before exit.

Q: Are points taxable?
A: Redemptions may attract perquisite taxation as per prevailing rules,
reflected in payroll.

Policy code: AHA-FAQ-2026-01 | Owner: Rewards & Recognition team.

# Aha Milestone & Long-Service Awards

## Milestones
Awards are granted at 5, 10, 15, 20 and 25 years of service.

## Award Types
Milestone awards include points, a certificate and a memento as per the
tenure tier.

## Recognition Ceremony
Awards are presented at the annual town hall or regional recognition events.

## Eligibility
Service continuity requirements apply; breaks are handled as per the tenure
calculation rules.

Policy code: AHA-MILE-2026-01 | Owner: Rewards & Recognition team.

# Aha Points Earning Matrix

## Business Wins
- Successful referral hired: 5,000 points.
- Qualifying cross-sell win: 250 points per unit.
- Audit-clean month for branch/ops team: 500 points.

## Recognition
- Regional CSAT topper: 1,500 points.
- Spot award (manager-issued): 250-1,000 points.
- Long-service milestones: tiered as per tenure.

## Development
- Approved certification pass: 2,000 points.
- Knowledge-sharing session delivered: 300 points.

## Campaigns
Quarterly campaigns publish boosted categories with limited-period
multipliers.

Policy code: AHA-EARN-2026-01 | Owner: Rewards & Recognition team.

# Aha Portal User Guide

## Login
Access the Aha portal with corporate credentials. First login prompts for a
redemption profile setup.

## Dashboard
The dashboard shows point balance, expiring points, recent transactions and
featured redemptions.

## Earning
Points accrue from referrals, cross-sell wins, certifications and
recognition as per the earning matrix.

## Redemption
Browse the catalogue, add items to the cart and check out. E-vouchers are
delivered by email; physical items ship to the registered address.

Policy code: AHA-PORTAL-2026-01 | Owner: Rewards & Recognition team.

# Aha — Employee Rewards Programme

## What is Aha?
Aha is the employee-facing rewards and recognition platform. Points are
earned through business-aligned actions and can be redeemed for vouchers,
merchandise and experiences on the Aha portal.

## Earning Points
| Trigger | Points |
|---|---|
| Successful employee referral hired | 5,000 |
| Cross-sell win (per qualifying win) | 250 |
| Audit-clean month (branch or ops team) | 500 |
| CSAT topping the region | 1,500 |
| Certification pass (approved list) | 2,000 |

## Redemption
- Minimum redemption balance: 1,000 points.
- Points expire 24 months after being awarded.
- Redemption catalogue: Amazon, Flipkart, Myntra vouchers, curated experiences,
  branded merchandise.

## Anti-Abuse Controls
- Referrals that leave within 6 months are clawed back automatically.
- Fake cross-sell entries are flagged during quarterly audit and lead to
  point reversal and disciplinary action.

## Support
For Aha portal issues, raise a ticket via HResponse under `Aha > Portal`.
For point disputes, use `Aha > Point Reversal`.

# Aha Quarterly Campaigns

## Structure
Each quarter runs a themed campaign with boosted categories, e.g. referral
months, service-excellence sprints or certification drives.

## Participation
Campaigns auto-track eligible actions. No separate enrolment is needed
unless specified in the campaign brief.

## Leaderboards
Optional leaderboards publish regional or team standings with the
participants' consent.

## Payout
Campaign points credit within 30 days of campaign close.

Policy code: AHA-CAMP-2026-01 | Owner: Rewards & Recognition team.

# Aha Redemption Catalogue

## Categories
- E-vouchers: retail, food, travel and wellness brands.
- Merchandise: electronics, home and lifestyle.
- Experiences: curated events and activities.
- Giving: donate points to approved causes.

## Value
Redemption values are published in points per item. Values refresh quarterly
with catalogue updates.

## Delivery
E-vouchers deliver instantly. Physical items ship within 7-10 business days
to the registered address.

## Expiry
Points expire 24 months after award. Expiring points are flagged on the
dashboard 60 days in advance.

Policy code: AHA-REDEEM-2026-01 | Owner: Rewards & Recognition team.

# Aha Spot Awards

## Purpose
Spot awards recognise exceptional contribution between appraisal cycles.

## Issuance
Managers may issue spot awards up to the defined point cap per quarter,
with a short citation.

## Approval
Awards above the manager cap require the next-level approver. HR samples
awards for quality and fairness.

## Visibility
Spot awards are visible to the recipient and their manager. Team-wide
announcements are optional.

Policy code: AHA-SPOT-2026-01 | Owner: Rewards & Recognition team.

# Aha Team Awards

## Categories
- Team of the quarter.
- Collaboration award for cross-functional delivery.
- Customer-impact award.

## Nomination
Nominations open quarterly with business-head endorsement. Teams self-nominate
with a delivery narrative.

## Evaluation
A cross-functional panel scores nominations on impact, collaboration and
customer outcomes.

## Reward
Winning teams receive points per member and a team celebration budget.

Policy code: AHA-TEAM-2026-01 | Owner: Rewards & Recognition team.

# Agent Console Guide

## Layout
The console shows the customer card, interaction history, queue state and
next booking in one view.

## Wrap-Up
Agents dispose every call with a disposition code and a CRM summary before
the next interaction.

## Transfers
Warm transfers preserve context to the receiving agent. Cold transfers need
supervisor approval for priority queues.

## Compliance
Calls are recorded; scripts for disclosures and verifications are mandatory
where defined.

Policy code: AP-CON-2026-01 | Owner: Contact Centre Technology.

# Callback SLA Framework

## Slots and SLA
- Priority/Burgundy: within 15 minutes of the slot.
- Retail: within 60 minutes of the slot.

## Measurement
SLA is measured from slot start to agent connect. Misses count against the
SLA dashboard.

## Breach Handling
Breaches trigger automatic retry, supervisor alerts and root-cause review
for repeat patterns.

## Reporting
Weekly SLA dashboards publish by queue, topic and agent team.

Policy code: AP-SLA-2026-01 | Owner: Assisted Channels team.

# CSAT Survey Programme

## Trigger
An SMS survey follows every completed call and callback.

## Questions
One CSAT rating question, one agent-empathy question and an optional
comment.

## Targets
Channel CSAT targets are set quarterly. Results feed agent coaching and
process improvement.

## Closed Loop
Detractors receive a follow-up within 48 hours from the service recovery
team.

Policy code: AP-CSAT-2026-01 | Owner: Assisted Channels team.

# Call Disposition Codes

## Code Families
- RES: resolved in first contact.
- FUP: follow-up scheduled.
- TRF: transferred.
- CMP: complaint registered.
- CBK: callback booked.
- NR: no response / voicemail.

## Usage Rules
Every interaction requires one disposition code. Follow-ups must reference
the original interaction ID.

## Reporting
Disposition data feeds first-contact-resolution and repeat-contact metrics.

Policy code: AP-DISP-2026-01 | Owner: Contact Centre Technology.

# Escalation Matrix

## Levels
1. Agent: first contact resolution.
2. Team lead: within same day for unresolved cases.
3. Relationship manager: priority customers.
4. Grievance officer: regulatory or media-flagged cases.

## Timeframes
Each level carries a defined SLA. Missed timeframes escalate automatically.

## Documentation
Every escalation records reason, owner and next action in the CRM.

Policy code: AP-ESC-2026-01 | Owner: Assisted Channels team.

# Axis Phone Feature Overview

## What It Is
Axis Phone is the assisted-service channel where customers request callbacks
from relationship managers and contact-centre agents.

## Core Features
- 30-minute callback slots between 09:00 and 20:00 IST.
- Topic-based routing: accounts, loans, cards, wealth, complaints.
- Language preference support including English, Hindi and regional languages.
- SMS confirmation with a callback reference ID.

## Channels
Callbacks can be requested from the mobile app, internet banking and the
वार्तालाप assistant.

Policy code: AP-OV-2026-01 | Owner: Assisted Channels team.

# IVR Tree & Routing

## Inbound Structure
1. Language selection.
2. Service selection: accounts, cards, loans, wealth, complaints.
3. Authentication via account details or OTP.
4. Routing to the topic queue.

## Smart Routing
Repeat callers are routed to the same agent when available. Priority and
Burgundy customers bypass general queues.

## Queue Messaging
Estimated wait is announced and callback-from-queue is offered beyond the
threshold.

Policy code: AP-IVR-2026-01 | Owner: Contact Centre Technology.

# Language Support Framework

## Supported Languages
English, Hindi, Marathi, Gujarati, Tamil, Telugu, Kannada, Bengali and
Malayalam in assisted channels.

## Preference Capture
Language preference is captured at booking and honoured in routing.

## Agent Matching
The routing engine matches language capability of agents to customer
preference. Overflow uses translation support with disclosure.

## Quality
Calls in regional languages are sampled for quality assurance with
language-certified auditors.

Policy code: AP-LANG-2026-01 | Owner: Assisted Channels team.

# Priority Customer Handling

## Tiers
Priority and Burgundy customers receive dedicated queues and shorter
callbacks.

## SLA
- Priority: callback within 15 minutes of the chosen slot.
- Retail: within 60 minutes.

## Dedicated Teams
Senior agents and relationship teams handle priority queues with warm
context handover from digital channels.

## Escalation
Unresolved priority interactions escalate to the relationship team within
24 hours.

Policy code: AP-PRIO-2026-01 | Owner: Assisted Channels team.

# Callback Scheduling Guide

## Slot Booking
Customers pick a 30-minute window between 09:00 and 20:00 IST on the next
five working days.

## Confirmation
An SMS confirms the slot with a reference ID. The agent sees the booking in
the agent console.

## Rescheduling
Customers can reschedule up to 30 minutes before the slot via the app or the
confirmation SMS link.

## Missed Calls
Missed callbacks retry once automatically, then flag for supervisor
follow-up the next business day.

Policy code: AP-SCH-2026-01 | Owner: Assisted Channels team.

# Axis Phone — Callback Workflow

## What is Axis Phone?
Axis Phone is the assisted-service channel where relationship managers and
contact-centre agents can be requested to call the customer back at a chosen
slot.

## Requesting a Callback (customer path)
1. Customer selects `Axis Phone` in the assistant or on the mobile app.
2. Provides preferred slot (30-minute windows between 09:00 and 20:00 IST).
3. Provides callback number (defaults to the number on file).
4. Selects the topic — `Account queries`, `Loan advisory`, `Cards`,
   `Wealth advisory`, `Complaint`, `Other`.
5. Receives an SMS confirmation with the callback reference ID.

## Assignment
The workflow engine picks an agent by:
- Topic → queue mapping.
- Customer segment (Retail / Priority / Burgundy).
- Language preference (English / Hindi / Regional).
- Agent load balancing — least-active-eligible agent wins.

## SLA
- Priority / Burgundy: **within 15 minutes** of the requested slot.
- Retail: **within 60 minutes**.
- Missed callbacks trigger an auto retry once and are flagged for supervisor
  review.

## Post-Call
- Agent must dispose the call with a valid outcome code and add the call
  summary in the CRM.
- CSAT survey SMS goes out within 30 minutes of call disposition.

## Reference
`AP-CB-2026-01` · Owner: Assisted Channels team.

# Dashboard Catalogue

## Executive
Daily performance snapshot: balances, disbursals, transactions and
exceptions.

## Business Line Dashboards
- Retail assets: disbursement, delinquency, collections.
- Cards: acquisition, spends, rewards, attrition.
- Payments: success rates, failures, chargebacks.

## Support Dashboards
- Data quality and pipeline health.
- Conversational BI usage and answer accuracy.

## Access
Dashboards are role-scoped. New dashboards follow the reporting request
workflow.

Policy code: BI-DASH-2026-01 | Owner: Business Analytics CoE.

# Data Freshness SLAs

## Tiers
- T0 (real-time/near-real-time): payment and fraud views, up to 15 minutes.
- T1 (daily): business performance and customer metrics, by 09:00 IST.
- T2 (weekly/monthly): HR and survey aggregates.

## Visibility
Each dashboard shows its last refresh timestamp. The assistant quotes
data-as-of dates in answers.

## Breach Handling
Freshness breaches alert the data engineering on-call and are tracked to
resolution.

Policy code: BI-FRESH-2026-01 | Owner: Data Platform team.

# BI Data Models

## Subject Areas
- Liabilities and assets (CASA, deposits, loans).
- Cards (spends, payments, rewards).
- Payments (UPI, NEFT/RTGS, mandates).
- Customer 360 (demographics, products, interactions).
- Branch and channel performance.
- HR and workforce metrics.

## Modelling Conventions
Fact tables use additive measures; dimensions conform across subject areas.
Calendar is the common conformed dimension.

## Definitions
Every measure carries an approved definition, owner and refresh timestamp
visible in the data dictionary.

Policy code: BI-MODEL-2026-01 | Owner: Data Platform team.

# BI Governance Framework

## Roles
- Data owners: accountable for definitions and quality.
- Data stewards: maintain the dictionary and lineage.
- BI consumers: use approved assets only.

## Change Control
Metric definitions, model changes and new dashboards follow the change
board process with impact assessment.

## Quality
Data-quality rules run at load. Scores publish on the quality dashboard.

## Review
The BI governance council reviews assets, usage and access quarterly.

Policy code: BI-GOV-2026-01 | Owner: Data Governance.

# Conversational BI — Getting Started

## What It Is
The `Conversational BI` bubble routes natural-language questions to the
Text-to-SQL agent, which drafts SQL against the reporting data mart, executes
it read-only, and returns a formatted result set.

## Available Datasets
- `customers` — one row per customer, with segment, branch, onboarding date.
- `accounts` — one row per account, product, balance, status.
- `transactions` — one row per transaction, txn_type, channel, amount.

Additional derived views are added quarterly; see the DDL under
`FINANCIAL_ADVISOR/mutual_funds.md` etc. for illustrative examples.

## Good Prompts
- "How many customers opened SAVINGS accounts?"
- "Top 5 customers by savings balance in Mumbai branches."
- "Average NEFT transaction amount last month by channel."
- "List customers with dormant SAVINGS accounts and balance under 5000."

## Guardrails
The engine will refuse to run SQL that:
- Writes data (INSERT / UPDATE / DELETE / DROP / ALTER / ATTACH).
- References tables outside the whitelisted set.
- Returns more than 5,000 rows in a single call.

## Limitations
- Text2SQL cannot answer questions that depend on documents (use the RAG
  bubbles for those).
- It does not yet handle time-series joins across all history — restrict to
  90 days for stable results.

## Reference
`CBI-INTRO-2026-01` · Owner: BI Platform team.

# KPI Definitions

## Business KPIs
- CASA ratio: CASA deposits / total deposits.
- Net interest margin: net interest income / average interest-earning assets.
- Credit cost: provisions / average advances.
- Cost-to-income: operating expenses / operating income.

## Customer KPIs
- Active rate: active customers / total customers over 90 days.
- Digital adoption: digital transactors / active customers.
- Net promoter score: promoters minus detractors, survey-based.

## Quality Rules
KPIs are versioned. Changes are approved by the KPI governance council.

Policy code: BI-KPI-2026-01 | Owner: Business Analytics CoE.

# BI Platform Architecture

## Layers
1. Sources: core banking, CRM, cards, payments and HR systems.
2. Lakehouse: raw, curated and semantic layers on the analytics platform.
3. Serving: semantic models consumed by dashboards, notebooks and the
   conversational BI assistant.

## Data Flow
Change-data-capture and batch pipelines land data within defined freshness
SLAs. Transformations produce the curated and semantic layers.

## Access Paths
The conversational BI assistant reads only the semantic layer. No query
touches source systems directly.

## Resilience
Pipelines carry retries, dead-letter handling and data-quality gates.

Policy code: BI-ARCH-2026-01 | Owner: Data Platform team.

# Query Guardrails for Conversational BI

## Safety Rules
- Only SELECT queries are generated; no writes or DDL.
- Row limits cap result sizes.
- Query timeouts kill runaway requests.
- Cost limits bind warehouse consumption per session.

## Sensitive Data
The semantic layer masks or excludes raw PAN, account numbers and
customer identifiers unless the user's role permits them.

## Audit
Every generated query, result and user interaction is logged with the
user ID and timestamp.

Policy code: BI-GUARD-2026-01 | Owner: Data Platform team.

# Row-Level Security

## Purpose
Row-level security ensures users see only the data their role permits.

## Dimensions
- Geography: zone, region, branch.
- Business: product lines and segments.
- Customer tiers: priority, retail, SME.

## Enforcement
RLS is enforced in the semantic layer, so dashboards and the assistant
inherit identical restrictions.

## Changes
RLS changes route through the data access request workflow with owner
approval.

Policy code: BI-RLS-2026-01 | Owner: Data Governance.

# Sample Conversational Queries

## Customer Metrics
"Show savings account balance trend for the last six months by region."

## Cards
"What was credit card spend last quarter compared to the previous quarter?"

## Branch Performance
"List the bottom five branches by current-account acquisition this month."

## Payments
"How many UPI transactions failed yesterday by failure code?"

## HR
"Show attrition rate for grade AVP and above in the last two quarters."

## Tips
Mention the measure, dimension and time window explicitly for best results.

Policy code: BI-QUERY-2026-01 | Owner: Data Platform team.

# Conversational BI Training Guide

## Getting Started
Start with the sample questions and the data dictionary walkthrough.

## Asking Better Questions
- Name the measure: balance, disbursal, spend, activation.
- Add dimensions: region, branch, product, month.
- State the window: yesterday, last quarter, FY-to-date.

## Understanding Answers
Answers cite the semantic model and data-as-of timestamp. Verify unusual
results against the source dashboard.

## Support
Queries, feedback and corrections route through the BI support queue.

Policy code: BI-TRAIN-2026-01 | Owner: Business Analytics CoE.

# Audit Trail Requirements for Changes

## What Must Be Logged
Every CR action: creation, edits, approvals, rejections, implementation
steps and closure, with actor, role and timestamp.

## Immutability
Audit logs are append-only. Administrative changes to logs are themselves
logged.

## Retention
Change records and logs are retained per the records retention policy
and made available to audit.

## Non-Compliance
Missing or altered audit trails are treated as a compliance breach.

Policy code: CR-AUDIT-2026-01 | Owner: Change Management Office.

# CAB Roles & Responsibilities

## Chair
The CAB chair convenes meetings, arbitrates conflicts and owns the
agenda.

## Members
Representatives from infrastructure, applications, security, business
units and the service desk.

## Duties
- Review and approve changes within authority.
- Review emergency-change retrospectives.
- Escalate policy violations.

## Cadence
Standing CAB meets twice weekly; emergency CAB convenes on demand.

Policy code: CR-CAB-2026-01 | Owner: Change Management Office.

# Change Approval Matrix

## Approval Levels
- Standard: team lead.
- Normal, medium risk: CAB with business representative.
- Normal, high risk: CAB plus business head.
- Emergency: two on-call approvers.

## Segregation
Implementers cannot approve their own changes. Approvers must be outside
the delivery team.

## Evidence
Approvals are recorded in the tool with timestamps and approver identity.

## Delegation
Approval delegation is defined per role in the matrix and reviewed
annually.

Policy code: CR-APPR-2026-01 | Owner: Change Management Office.

# Change Automation Guidelines

## Scope
Automation covers CI/CD deployment pipelines, infrastructure-as-code and
self-service standard changes.

## Governance
Automated changes remain governed by the same approval matrix; standard
changes may use pre-approved templates.

## Guardrails
- Automated tests as gates.
- Immutable audit logs.
- Automatic rollback triggers on failure thresholds.

## Exclusions
High-risk and regulatory-impacting changes remain manual unless
specifically approved for automation.

Policy code: CR-AUTO-2026-01 | Owner: DevOps Enablement.

# Change Calendar Management

## Purpose
The calendar sequences approved changes to avoid resource conflicts and
landing-zone contention.

## Slotting Rules
- No more than the prescribed number of production changes per window.
- Dependency-linked changes are scheduled together.
- High-risk changes are isolated from other high-risk changes.

## Conflict Resolution
Calendar conflicts are escalated to the Change Management Office, which
arbitrates based on business priority.

## Visibility
The calendar is published and visible to all delivery teams.

Policy code: CR-CAL-2026-01 | Owner: Change Management Office.

# Change Freeze Calendar

## Freeze Periods
- Financial year-end: last 5 business days of March.
- Half-year close: last 3 business days of September.
- RBI-mandated reporting windows.
- Major festival sale periods for customer-facing systems.

## Exceptions
Freeze exceptions require CIO approval and must be logged as emergency
changes.

## Communication
The freeze calendar is published annually and revised as needed.

Policy code: CR-FREEZE-2026-01 | Owner: Change Management Office.

# Change Management (CR) — Standard Process

## Change Categories
| Category | Definition | Approval |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Standard | Pre-approved template, low risk | Team Lead |
| Normal | Business change with a defined blast radius | CAB |
| Emergency | Production incident fix within 24 hours | Emergency CAB |

## Required Artefacts
Every CR must attach:
1. Business justification and scope.
2. Impact assessment (customer facing? cross-team? regulator? data-migration?).
3. Roll-out plan with owners.
4. Roll-back plan verified in the last drill.
5. Test evidence — unit, integration, UAT.
6. Communication plan (mailer templates, banner text).

## CAB Cadence
- Standing CAB every **Tuesday and Thursday, 16:00 IST**.
- Cut-off for CR submission is 24 hours before CAB.
- Emergency CRs are triaged on demand via the emergency channel.

## Blackout Windows
No non-emergency production changes during:
- Financial year-end (last 5 business days of March).
- Half-year close (last 3 business days of September).
- RBI mandated reporting windows.

## Reference
`CR-STD-2026-01` · Owner: Change Advisory Board.

# Change Request (CR) Standard

## Definition
A **Change Request** is any planned addition, modification or removal of a
production or production-adjacent component that could affect service
availability, integrity or compliance.

## CR Categories
| Category | Approval | Freeze windows apply? |
|---|---|---|
| Standard | Pre-approved template, no CAB | Yes |
| Normal | CAB approval | Yes |
| Emergency | Emergency CAB (E-CAB) | Yes, with waiver |

## Mandatory CR Fields
- Business justification.
- Impact assessment (services, users, data).
- Roll-back plan with owner and time budget.
- Test evidence (unit, integration, UAT sign-off).
- Communication plan.
- Downtime window (if any).

## Freeze Windows
No production CRs during:
- Financial year-end close (last week of March, first week of April).
- Half-yearly close (last week of September, first week of October).
- Regulatory reporting window (2 business days before submission deadline).

## Approval Matrix
| Change scope | Approver |
|---|---|
| Non-prod, single team | Team lead |
| Prod, single service | Service owner |
| Prod, cross-service or data | CAB |
| Regulatory / customer-facing | CAB + Compliance sign-off |

## References
- Standard code: CR-STD-2026-01
- Owner: Change Advisory Board (CAB) secretariat.

# Configuration Management Basics

## CMDB Scope
The configuration management database records production assets, their
relationships and owners.

## CI Attributes
Each configuration item carries owner, environment, criticality, and
dependency attributes.

## Change Linkage
Changes must reference affected configuration items. The CMDB updates
on implementation.

## Accuracy
CMDB accuracy is measured quarterly; critical-item accuracy below the
threshold triggers remediation.

Policy code: CR-CMDB-2026-01 | Owner: IT Service Management.

# CR KPIs & Metrics

## Key Metrics
- Successful change rate.
- Unplanned/emergency change ratio.
- Change-induced incident rate.
- Post-implementation review completion.
- Calendar adherence.

## Targets
Targets are set annually by the Change Management Office and reviewed
with CAB monthly.

## Reporting
A monthly change dashboard is published to senior management.

## Drill-Down
Metrics drill to individual changes for root-cause analysis.

Policy code: CR-KPI-2026-01 | Owner: Change Management Office.

# Change Request Lifecycle

## Stages
1. Draft: business case and impact assessment.
2. Review: technical and risk review with peer checks.
3. Approval: CAB or emergency CAB as applicable.
4. Implementation: within the approved window.
5. Post-implementation review and closure.

## State Transitions
Only approved roles may move a CR between states. Every transition is
logged with the actor and timestamp.

## Rejection and Rework
Rejected CRs are returned with reasons. Reworked CRs re-enter review
without losing history.

## Closure
A CR closes only after successful implementation, rollback readiness expiry
and documentation of outcomes.

Policy code: CR-LIFE-2026-01 | Owner: Change Management Office.

# CR Templates & Mandatory Fields

## Standard Template
- Change title and unique ID.
- Category: standard, normal, emergency.
- Business justification and impacted services.
- Risk assessment and rollback plan.
- Implementation window and owner.

## Field Completeness
A CR cannot be submitted with missing mandatory fields. The tool validates
completeness before routing.

## Evidence Attachments
Test results, approvals and communication drafts attach to the CR before
CAB review.

## Template Updates
Templates are reviewed annually by the Change Management Office.

Policy code: CR-TPL-2026-01 | Owner: Change Management Office.

# Deployment Windows

## Standard Windows
Production deployments run in the night maintenance window: 00:00 to
04:00 IST, unless otherwise approved.

## Exceptions
Customer-impacting daytime changes require business-head and CAB
approval with documented mitigation.

## Window Discipline
Deployments must complete within the window. Runaway deployments are
halted and rolled back per the runbook.

## Weekend Deployments
Weekend deployments are permitted only for approved releases and require
on-call support coverage.

Policy code: CR-WIN-2026-01 | Owner: Release Management Office.

# Emergency Change Process

## Definition
Emergency changes address production incidents requiring immediate
remediation, where waiting for CAB would extend impact.

## Initiation
The incident commander opens an emergency CR with the incident ID linked.

## Approval
Emergency approval requires two approvers from the on-call list, one of
whom is a manager or above.

## Retrospective
Every emergency change undergoes post-implementation review within 5
working days. Unplanned work is reported to CAB.

## Controls
Abuse of the emergency route (pre-planned work logged as emergency) is a
compliance breach.

Policy code: CR-EMER-2026-01 | Owner: Change Management Office.

# Environment Strategy

## Environments
Dev, QA, staging and production with defined promotion rules.

## Parity
Staging mirrors production configuration for the change class being
tested. Drift is reconciled before deployment.

## Data
Test environments use masked or synthetic data. Production data in
non-production environments requires approval.

## Access
Environment access follows least privilege; production access is
break-glass controlled.

Policy code: CR-ENV-2026-01 | Owner: Release Management Office.

# Impact Assessment Checklist

## Dimensions
- Customer: which journeys and channels are affected.
- Systems: upstream and downstream dependencies.
- Data: schema, migration and retention impact.
- Regulatory: reporting and audit implications.
- Operations: runbook and support readiness.

## Scoring
Changes are scored low, medium or high risk from the assessment. Score
drives the approval route.

## Review

Recurrence rate, mean time to problem resolution and open-problem aging

Know Your Customer (KYC) is the collection of laws, regulations and guidelines
that require regulated financial businesses to verify the identity, suitability
and risks associated with maintaining a business relationship with a customer.
These procedures fit within the broader scope of Anti-Money Laundering (AML)
and Counter-Terrorism Financing (CTF) regulations.

Modern KYC frameworks are built on three pillars:

- **Customer Identification Program (CIP)** — legally mandated verification of
  any person or entity opening a new account, including name, date of birth,
  address and a government-issued identification number.
- **Customer Due Diligence (CDD)** — understanding the nature and purpose of a
  client relationship, developing a risk profile, and ongoing monitoring of
  transactions for suspicious activity.
- **Enhanced Due Diligence (EDD)** — extra checks for higher risk clients such
  as politically exposed persons (PEPs), cross-border correspondent banking
  relationships, or businesses operating in jurisdictions with strategic
  deficiencies in their AML/CFT regimes.

Regulated entities are required to maintain a written, risk-based KYC program
that: forms a reasonable belief that they know the true identity of every
customer; verifies identity within a reasonable time; checks the customer
against sanctions and terror watchlists; and retains records for a defined
period after account closure (typically five years).

Electronic KYC (eKYC) uses digital identity verification, biometric checks and
liveness detection to onboard customers remotely. In India, the Reserve Bank of
India first issued KYC guidelines for banks in 2002; video KYC (V-CIP) is
permitted for eligible savings account onboarding, subject to procedural
controls around live capture, random challenge and geo-tagging.

# Background: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)

Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) is a technique that enables large
language models (LLMs) to retrieve and incorporate new information from
external data sources at inference time, instead of relying solely on their
pre-training data.

At a high level, a RAG system operates in three stages:

1. **Indexing.** External data (documents, tables, knowledge graphs) is
   converted into vector embeddings and stored in a vector database.
2. **Retrieval.** For a given user query, a retriever selects the most
   relevant documents from the vector store. Reranking, hybrid search
   (sparse + dense) and late-interaction models such as ColBERT are common
   accuracy improvements.
3. **Generation.** The retrieved passages are supplied to the LLM through
   prompt engineering ("prompt stuffing"), so the model prioritises the
   retrieved context over its parametric memory when producing an answer.

RAG improves factuality, allows citing sources for verification, and removes
the need to retrain the base model when knowledge changes. It does not
eliminate hallucinations: models can still misinterpret retrieved context,
combine outdated and updated information, or generate false claims when
retrieval quality is poor ("RAG poisoning"). Robust RAG systems therefore
depend heavily on chunking strategy, retriever quality, reranking, and
downstream guardrails.

# Network Troubleshooting Playbook

## Wi-Fi / LAN Not Working
1. Check the physical cable / dock is seated firmly.
2. `Windows key + I → Network & Internet → Advanced → Network reset`.
3. Try a different port or the guest wifi to isolate infra vs. laptop.
4. If still failing, open Unidesk under `IT Helpdesk > Connectivity > Wired/Wireless`.

## VPN Disconnect Loop
- Confirm you are on the corporate VPN group in Anyconnect (not the guest
  group).
- Toggle **Airplane mode** for 10 seconds to refresh the network stack.
- Clear the VPN posture cache (`%ProgramData%\Cisco\AnyConnect\posture\ISEPosture.cfg`) and re-launch.
- If disconnects persist within 60 seconds of connect, log a P2 SR — likely
  a certificate issue.

## Slow Application Load
Order of triage:
1. Ping the app endpoint from a command prompt; RTT > 200ms indicates
   backbone congestion.
2. Check `Task Manager > Performance` — is disk I/O at 100%? Might be a
   background AV scan.
3. Check DNS — `nslookup finacle.internal` should return a 10.x address.
4. Clear browser cache & retry.

# Anti-Money Laundering (AML) — Operating Framework

## Purpose
The AML framework prevents the bank's channels being used to launder proceeds
of crime and to finance terrorism, in line with the Prevention of Money
Laundering Act (PMLA), 2002 and RBI Master Direction on KYC.

## Three Lines of Defence
- **1st line — Business units:** onboard customers correctly, monitor
  transactions, escalate red flags.
- **2nd line — Financial Crime Compliance (FCC):** owns the AML policy,
  runs the sanctions and PEP screening tools, files STRs.
- **3rd line — Internal Audit:** independently tests the framework annually.

## Customer Risk Categorisation
- **Low risk:** salaried resident individuals with no adverse hits.
- **Medium risk:** self-employed, high-net-worth individuals, non-resident
  individuals with low transaction velocity.
- **High risk:** NGOs, cash-intensive businesses, PEPs, customers in
  FATF-listed jurisdictions.

Risk category drives periodic KYC refresh frequency (see the KYC standard).

## Reporting Obligations
| Report | Threshold | Filing SLA |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Cash Transaction Report (CTR) | Cash > ₹10L / day per customer | 15th of the following month |
| Suspicious Transaction Report (STR) | On red flag | 7 working days from detection |
| Counterfeit Currency Report (CCR) | Any incident | 7 working days |
| Cross-Border Wire Transfer Report (CBWTR) | > ₹5L | 15th of the following month |

## Training
All customer-facing staff must complete the annual AML e-learning by
30 September of each year. Non-completion is tracked as an audit finding.

## Reference
`LAW-AML-2026-02` · Owner: Financial Crime Compliance unit.

Suspected bribery is reported through the whistleblower channel. Non-compliance
may result in termination and regulatory reporting.

Security events are detected through monitoring tools, staff reports and vendor
alerts. Every suspected personal-data breach is logged as a Priority-Zero incident.

## Containment
Containment includes isolating affected systems, revoking compromised credentials
and preserving forensic evidence without modification.

## Notification
Notifiable breaches are reported to the Data Protection Board within 72 hours
under the DPDP framework, and affected data principals are informed promptly.

## Investigation
Root-cause analysis is completed within 15 working days. Corrective actions are
tracked to closure with the Chief Information Security Officer.

## Review
The breach register is reviewed quarterly by the Risk Management Committee.

# Data Privacy — DPDP Act 2023 Alignment

## What the DPDP Act Requires
The Digital Personal Data Protection (DPDP) Act, 2023 defines how personal
data of Indian citizens ("Data Principals") must be processed by any entity
("Data Fiduciary"). Axis Bank is a Significant Data Fiduciary and follows the
obligations below.

## Lawful Grounds for Processing
Bank processes personal data only on one of the following grounds:
- Explicit consent obtained through the customer journey.
- Legitimate use for the performance of a service the customer has requested.
- Compliance with applicable laws (RBI Master Directions, PMLA, income tax
  reporting).
- Employment obligations for staff data.

## Data Principal Rights
Customers can raise these requests through the customer portal or by writing
to `dpo@axisbank.com`:
- Right to information about processing.
- Right to correction of inaccurate data.
- Right to erasure (subject to statutory retention).
- Right to grievance redressal (30 day SLA).
- Right to nominate a person to exercise their rights.

## Retention
Customer KYC and transaction data are retained for a **minimum of 8 years**
after account closure per PMLA. Beyond that, data is anonymised or purged
unless a legal hold is in effect.

## Data Breach Handling
Any suspected breach must be reported to the DPO within 24 hours by raising
a `Priority-Zero` incident on Unidesk. The DPO reports notifiable breaches to
the Data Protection Board within 72 hours.

## Reference
`LAW-DPDP-2026-01` · Owner: Data Protection Office (DPO).

extends to the aggregate of a depositor's accounts with the same bank.

Inter-bank deposits, government deposits and deposits of foreign governments
are excluded.

## Claim Process
In a liquidation scenario, DICGC settles claims up to the insured amount within
prescribed timelines.

Branches display DICGC coverage information and respond to customer queries on
the scheme.

Records are retained for legal, regulatory, tax and business needs and disposed
of thereafter through an approved process.

## Retention Classes
- KYC and transaction records: as per PMLA requirements.
- Tax records: as per Income-Tax Act.
- Employment records: as per labour statutes.
- Contracts: for the contract term plus limitation periods.

Consent for processing personal data must be free, specific, informed,
unconditional and unambiguous, with clear affirmative action.

Every consent request describes the personal data collected, purpose, rights of
the data principal and grievance mechanism in clear, plain language.

after withdrawal, subject to statutory retention obligations.

Consent records with timestamps and versions are retained as evidence of lawful

current and capital account dealings.

Reports include complete identifiers, transaction details, account references

The bank preserves underlying records and responds to FIU-IND requisitions
within prescribed timelines.

Covers internal fraud, external fraud against customers, and cyber-fraud across

Designated persons file initial and continuous disclosures of holdings and trades

# Know Your Customer (KYC) Standard

## Purpose
This standard defines the mandatory identity and address verification a
banker must perform before onboarding any customer, in line with the RBI
Master Direction on KYC.

## Acceptable Officially Valid Documents (OVDs)
- Aadhaar (with masked number, per UIDAI guideline).
- PAN.
- Passport.
- Driving licence issued by an RTO.
- Voter ID issued by ECI.
- Job card issued by NREGA duly signed by the state government.

## Video KYC (V-CIP)
V-CIP is available for eligible savings account onboarding subject to:
- Genuine live video with the customer visible from mid-torso up.
- Random challenge (e.g., "Show your OVD now").
- Officer capturing at least 3 still frames during the call.
- Geo-tagging of the customer's location.

## Periodic Update Frequency
| Risk Category | Frequency |
|---|---|
| High risk | Every 2 years |
| Medium risk | Every 8 years |
| Low risk | Every 10 years |

## Deficient KYC
Accounts flagged with deficient KYC are moved to `PARTIAL FREEZE` after
two written reminders. All debits (excluding regulatory / statutory dues)
are blocked in this state.

## References
- Policy code: LAW-KYC-2026-01
- Aligned to RBI Master Direction on KYC (as amended).
- Owner: Compliance — Financial Crime unit.

Litigation notice, regulatory enquiry, audit requirement or anticipated
dispute triggers a legal hold.

Email, documents, chat, databases and paper records related to the matter.

On matter closure, Legal issues a release notice and normal retention resumes.

Failure to preserve under a hold is escalated as a compliance breach.

Products and communications must be fair, transparent and non-misleading.
Employees must not make promises outside approved product features.

appropriate product mapping with documented consent.

## Grievance Readiness
Customers receive clear pre-contractual disclosures including terms, charges
and grievance channels.

Mis-selling attracts disciplinary action and may be reported to regulators.

The Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881 governs cheques, promissory notes and
bills of exchange.

## Cheque Dishonour
Dishonoured cheques attract penalties and may lead to proceedings under
Section 138 upon statutory notice and non-payment within 15 days.

## Endorsement
Instruments are negotiated by endorsement and delivery. The bank verifies
endorsements per prescribed procedures.

Payment in due course protects the bank. Alterations material to the instrument
render it invalid unless authenticated.

Ops staff complete annual NI Act refreshers on dishonour handling and returns.

Outsourcing of material activities follows RBI guidelines on outsourcing of
financial services.

Activities are assessed for materiality based on impact on customers, data
confidentiality, regulatory reporting and business continuity.

## Board Oversight
Material outsourcing arrangements are approved by the board or its committee.
The outsourcing policy is reviewed annually.

## Service Provider Management
SLAs, audit rights, sub-contracting restrictions and exit clauses are mandated
in contracts.

The register of outsourcing arrangements is maintained centrally and available
to auditors and supervisors.

Payment operations follow the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007 and
RBI directions on digital payments.

## Authorisation
The bank operates approved payment systems — UPI, NEFT, RTGS, cards and wallets
— under board-approved policies.

Limits, cooling periods and dispute timelines follow RBI circulars. Unauthorised
transaction liability follows the zero/limited-liability framework.

Payment systems maintain defined availability targets, fallback arrangements
and regular recovery drills.

## Reporting
Periodic returns and incident notifications are filed with the RBI within
prescribed timelines.

The Prevention of Money Laundering Act, 2002 obligates the bank to detect,
deter and report money-laundering activity.

The Principal Officer is responsible for filings with FIU-IND. Every business
unit designates a compliance liaison.

## Transaction Monitoring
Automated and rule-based monitoring flags unusual patterns: structuring,
rapid movement, high-risk jurisdiction flows and unexpected activity.

Cash Transaction Reports, Suspicious Transaction Reports, Counterfeit Currency

timelines.

All customer-facing staff complete annual AML training; completion is tracked

Customer onboarding follows the RBI Master Direction on Know Your Customer,
2016 (as amended).

- Verify beneficial owners for non-individual customers.
- Assign a risk category: low, medium or high.

## Enhanced Due Diligence
EDD applies to PEPs, high-risk geographies and high-value or complex
transactions, including source-of-funds checks.

## Record Retention
KYC records are maintained for the prescribed period after account closure as
per PMLA requirements.

Calls in sales and service channels are recorded for quality, dispute
resolution and regulatory compliance.

Customers are informed of recording through IVR announcements and in
channel terms.

Recordings are encrypted, retained per the retention schedule and accessible
only to authorised roles.

Recordings may be used for quality monitoring, training, investigation and
regulatory response. They are never shared outside authorised processes.

# SARFAESI Overview for Staff

## Regulatory Basis
The Securitisation and Reconstruction of Financial Assets and Enforcement of
Security Interest Act, 2002 enables secured creditors to enforce security
interests without court intervention.

## Key Stages
- Classification of the account as NPA.
- Demand notice under Section 13(2) with a 60-day period.
- Possession, sale or transfer of secured assets if dues remain unpaid.

## Borrower Remedies
Borrowers may object to the notice, seek account review, and approach the
Debts Recovery Tribunal within prescribed timelines.

## Staff Conduct
Only trained recovery staff handle SARFAESI actions. Fair-practices codes for
recovery agents are strictly followed.

All court summons, subpoenas, and regulatory requisitions route through the
central legal intake inbox within 24 hours of receipt.

Legal coordinates with business, compliance and operations to compile
responses. Internal deadlines are set at least three days before external
deadlines.

## Confidentiality
Only authorised personnel handle the matter. Responding parties are restricted
to named custodians.

A register records the notice, response timeline, produced documents and
closure.

Applies to vendors, service providers, fintech partners and outsourcing
arrangements with access to bank data, systems or customers.

## Onboarding Diligence
Financial, operational, reputational, data-security and regulatory screening
before contract signing. High-risk categories require enhanced checks.

## Contractual Controls
Contracts include data-protection clauses, audit rights, business continuity
obligations and incident notification timelines.

Periodic re-assessment, SLA reviews and security posture checks. Critical
vendors are re-assessed at least annually.

Off-boarding includes data return/destruction certification and access
revocation verification.

## Core Checks
- Incorporation and existence verification.
- Ultimate beneficial ownership identification.
- Sanctions, negative news and litigation screening.
- Financial health assessment.

## Risk Tiers
Vendors are tiered by spend, data access and criticality. Tier-1 vendors face
the full due-diligence scope.

## Documentation
Due-diligence packs are retained for audit and refreshed annually or on
material change.

Failed due diligence leads to engagement rejection or termination with
business continuity support.

# Whistleblower Policy

## Purpose
The policy enables employees and third parties to report suspected misconduct,
fraud, regulatory violations or ethical breaches without fear of retaliation.

## Channels
Reports may be submitted through the dedicated whistleblower portal, email or
postal address managed by the ethics committee. Anonymous reporting is permitted.

## Confidentiality
The identity of the whistleblower is protected to the extent permitted by law.
Breach of confidentiality by investigation teams is a disciplinary offence.

## Protection
Good-faith reports do not attract adverse consequences. Vexatious or malicious
complaints are themselves subject to disciplinary action.

## Investigation
The ethics committee triages and investigates reports, engaging Internal Audit,
Compliance or external experts as needed. Outcomes are reported to the Audit
Committee of the Board.
